policy: Lifecycle classification records repository-tooling ownership and exact reviewed reachability only; it grants no credential access, business-data ownership, production write capability, provider access, telephony capability, or scan exemption.

surfaces.approved_architecture_path: container entrypoint that repairs ownership of the tg-bot data volume and drops privileges before executing the image command
surfaces.evidence: The exact ten-line POSIX shell script runs `set -eu`, `mkdir -p /app/data`, `chown -R app:app /app/data`, and `exec gosu app "$@"`. It exists because the tg_bot_data volume mount replaces /app/data and hides the ownership prepared at image build time, which would otherwise leave the unprivileged account unable to write the bot-local SQLite file. Both filesystem operations are confined to that one container-internal directory. The script reads no environment variable, opens no file, contacts no network, holds no database, provider or telephony client, and reaches no credential; its final action reduces privilege rather than raising it, handing control to the unchanged image command as the same non-root account used before. The tracked-surface scanner nevertheless conservatively enrolls every .sh file as an operational surface.
